Our Story

Three generations,
one long table.

Sefra started as a six-table room run by Hajjeh Mariam, who believed a guest should never see the bottom of a dish. Her son added the charcoal grill; her grandchildren added the dining room you see today — but the rule never changed.

Everything is made in-house each morning: the hummus is pounded, never blended to death; the kibbeh is shaped by hand; the bread comes off the saj to order. If a dish runs out, it runs out — we would rather say “khalas, bukra” than serve you yesterday's food.

— عيلة حداد، من ١٩٩٨

The dishes people cross the city for

Four plates that have been on the menu since the beginning — and the first to sell out on weekends.

Hummus Beiruti حمّص

Chickpeas, tahini, lemon — and the patience to get the ratio right. Finished with first-press olive oil from the south.

$6Since 1998

Mashawi Mshakkaleh مشاوي

Kofta, shish tawook and lamb kebab off the charcoal, on markouk bread with sumac onions and grilled tomato.

Fattoush فتّوش

Purslane when it's in season, radish, mint and fried pita under a sumac and pomegranate-molasses dressing.

Knefeh كنافة

The Menu

Eat in order: cold, hot, grill, sweet

Prices in USD. Bread, pickles and fresh mint come with everything — that's not a promotion, that's the house.

Allergies? Tell us before you order — most mezze can be made without nuts, and the grill is happy to go garlic-free (reluctantly).
